# Darknode

> Darknode finds the real security risks in a domain, code, dependencies and cloud configuration, ranks them by live exploitation data (CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS) rather than by an AI model's opinion, and gives a concrete fix for each. It starts with a free domain check that needs no sign-up.

Darknode runs in the browser (the Deck workspace at darknode.ai), as a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, and as a command-line tool (the Darknode CLI, which includes the Nexus terminal coding agent). Checks are deterministic: each result shows how it was reached. Use it only on systems you own or are authorized to assess.

Plans: Free ($0) includes the domain, email and certificate checks, the live vulnerability feed, one watched domain with email alerts, and the Darknode assistant at 50 messages a day. Pro ($29 per user a month) adds the exposure and application security tools, saved findings and reports, premium AI models, monitors and deadline clocks. Team ($79 per user a month) adds shared workspaces, roles and the organization tools. Enterprise is custom. Paid plans are in preview: checkout is not live yet, so upgrades are requested and granted by hand.

## Product

- [Home and free domain check](https://darknode.ai/): enter a domain to grade its email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), HTTPS, certificate expiry, security headers, DNSSEC, CAA and security.txt, with the fix for each failing check
- [Shareable check page](https://darknode.ai/check/example.com): the same check for one domain at a link you can share; it runs live each time it opens
- [Features](https://darknode.ai/features): what Darknode checks (known-exploited vulnerabilities, domain and email, attack surface, code and secrets, dependencies, cloud and infrastructure as code) and how it works
- [Pricing](https://darknode.ai/pricing): Free, Pro, Team and Enterprise, and what each includes
- [FAQ](https://darknode.ai/faq): plans, where code and data go, offline use, AI models, legal use

## Tools and products

- [Nexus](https://darknode.ai/nexus): the terminal coding agent in the Darknode CLI; one interface over six engines (Claude Code, the Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenCode, Aider and local Ollama models)
- [GenAI Security Crosswalk](https://darknode.ai/crosswalk): the OWASP GenAI security risks mapped to 26 security frameworks; free, no account needed
- [Security knowledge](https://darknode.ai/security-knowledge): OWASP Top 10, security patterns, cheat sheets, privilege escalation and network reconnaissance
- [Darknode OS](https://darknode.ai/darknode-os): a from-scratch x86 research kernel and an Ubuntu 24.04 desktop edition, both run in a virtual machine
- [Government and regulated teams](https://darknode.ai/government): control mapping, vulnerability deadlines with the BOD 22-01 clock, and audit evidence
- [Darknode CLI source](https://github.com/Darknode-Official/darknode-cli): install from source; includes Nexus and the `darknode mcp` server for MCP clients
